tools.name: civic.get_code_section
tools.description: Get the text of a Code of Virginia section by its citation (e.g. '1-500', '18.2-57'). Direct lookup only — this is not a full-text search; the caller must already know or have found the section number. Results carry the section's own citation history exactly as published, with a link to the live page. A missing section (repealed, renumbered, or never existed) returns found=False, not an error.

tools.name: geo.find_parcel
tools.description: Find parcel records in a Virginia jurisdiction by parcel PIN or by a lon/lat point. Pass the user's jurisdiction string as given — resolution and its ambiguities are handled here, and candidate lists must go back to the user unchosen. Results carry provenance and coverage; an empty result with coverage.registry='none' means Commonwealth has no source there, not that no parcel exists. For a street address, call geo.resolve_location first to get the jurisdiction and a coordinate.

tools.name: geo.find_zoning
tools.description: Find the zoning district(s) for a parcel PIN or lon/lat point in a Virginia jurisdiction. Screening only: results state the GIS layer's answer, never a legal determination — repeat the screening_only warning to the user. When two official sources are registered, both are queried and any disagreement is shown, not reconciled. Use geo.find_parcel first when you need the parcel record itself.

tools.name: geo.find_boundaries
tools.description: Get a Virginia jurisdiction's official boundary: FIPS, GNIS, area, jurisdiction type, bounding box, and the publisher's own centroid. Use to confirm WHICH government's territory is meant and how big it is. Independent cities are returned as their own territory, never as part of the county sharing their name. Screening geometry only — it is generalized and the publisher disclaims survey use, so never decide from it which side of a boundary an address sits on. Pass detail='full' for vertices. Not a containment test: to find which jurisdiction covers a point, use registry.resolve_jurisdiction with lon/lat.

tools.name: geo.find_address
tools.description: Find address-point records in a Virginia jurisdiction, by address string or by a lon/lat point. The string path is a PREFIX match on the publisher's own spelling ("6800 BEULAH ST"), not a fuzzy search — use geo.resolve_location when the input is a typed address that needs interpreting. A record's `po_name` is a POSTAL city and is never the government: a Fairfax County address reads "ALEXANDRIA". Read `locality` and `fips` for the jurisdiction. An empty result means this publisher has no record, which is not the same as no such address existing.

tools.name: geo.resolve_location
tools.description: Turn a Virginia street address or a 5-digit ZIP into the government that covers it. Use this FIRST when the user gives an address — the other tools take a jurisdiction name or a coordinate, not an address. An address is geocoded and the resulting point is placed by point-in-polygon; the geocoder's own city field is a POSTAL city and is never the answer (a Fairfax County address reads 'Alexandria'). A ZIP returns every locality it touches: ZIPs are delivery routes and cross government boundaries constantly, so a multi-locality ZIP comes back as candidates with requires_user_choice and must go to the user unchosen. Pass exactly one of `address` or `zip_code`.

tools.name: geo.find_buildings
tools.description: Find building footprints at a lon/lat point (with a radius) or on a parcel PIN in a Virginia jurisdiction. Answers 'is this ground built on, and how much of it'. An empty result is NOT evidence of vacant land — this is a derived layer whose coverage varies by locality. Height, storey, and class fields are frequently null, which means the publisher has no value. Footprint area is published in Web Mercator, where area is inflated about 1.6x at Virginia's latitudes; both the publisher's number and a converted approximation are returned, each labelled. A dense urban query truncates — narrow the radius rather than reading a short list as the whole answer.

tools.name: geo.find_landmarks
tools.description: Find named public places in a Virginia jurisdiction — schools, libraries, fire stations, DMV offices, state parks — by name prefix, by the publisher's own place_type vocabulary, or near a lon/lat point. NOT an inventory: a place missing from this layer may simply never have been added, so an empty result never means there is no school there. Each record names the organisation it came from, and that organisation is its authority, not the map publisher. Record URLs are returned as data and are never fetched. Pass at least one filter.

tools.name: geo.find_roads
tools.description: Find road segments and routes in a Virginia jurisdiction, by street-name prefix or near a lon/lat point. TWO official sources answer this and they are expected to disagree: VDOT's route inventory is a linear-referencing model with its own route names and measures, VGIN's centerlines are an aggregation of local submissions with segment-level detail. Both are returned unreconciled and the comparison block says whether their names agree — a difference is usually a difference in how the road is modelled, not an error. Centerlines are not right-of-way boundaries. A road along a locality line belongs to both localities in the results.

tools.name: geo.find_environmental_sites
tools.description: Find the environmental monitoring stations a Virginia agency has on record near a lon/lat point. READ THE LIMITS BEFORE USING THIS: it is NOT a complete inventory of environmental sites, and it is NOT a determination that any site is safe, contaminated, or suitable for a given use. What is registered today is DEQ's water-quality monitoring network — air, waste, and land programmes are not in it. A station on record means that spot is or was sampled and nothing more; historic stations are included, so read last_sample_date. An empty result means no station of that kind is on record near the point, never that the ground is clean. Say all of this to the user; do not summarise it away. A point is required — this source has no locality field.

tools.name: registry.resolve_jurisdiction
tools.description: Resolve a Virginia jurisdiction from a name, alias, or FIPS code, or from a lon/lat point by point-in-polygon against official boundaries. Use FIRST whenever a place is named or a coordinate is given: Virginia has independent cities that are not inside the counties sharing their names (Fairfax City is not in Fairfax County), and towns that sit inside a county so BOTH governments apply — read layered_authorities, do not assume the resolved leaf answers everything. Pass `query` OR lon/lat, never both. If the result carries candidates with requires_user_choice, present them to the user and never pick one yourself. For a street address or a ZIP, use geo.resolve_location instead.

tools.name: registry.search_sources
tools.description: Search the Government Source Registry: which registered public systems cover a capability or jurisdiction, with authority level and current state. Use to answer 'what does Commonwealth cover?' before assuming coverage. Not a data query tool — use the geo.* tools for actual records.

tools.name: registry.describe_source
tools.description: Full registry entry for one source id: publisher, authority, terms, limitations. Use when the user asks where an answer came from or what a source's caveats are.

tools.name: registry.source_status
tools.description: Declared and operational state for registered sources. Use when a query reported a source failure and you need to say whether the source is known-down.

sources.name: Charles City County Tax Parcels (GIS Open Data)
known_limitations: No zoning layer published for this jurisdiction; parcel.lookup only.
Only two fields exposed (OBJECTID, MAP_PIN) — no owner, valuation, or land-use attributes available through this source.

sources.name: Code of Virginia (law.lis.virginia.gov)
sources.publisher: Division of Legislative Automated Systems (DLAS), Virginia General Assembly
known_limitations: Direct citation lookup only — this reads one section page per call; there is no full-text search against this adapter (the site's own search feature was not reverse-engineered).
HTML-page scraping, not a structured API — a redesign of the site's markup would break parsing before it broke any published contract.
No machine-readable last-edit date per section; retrieval time is known, the underlying text's amendment date is only what the section's own citation-history paragraph states in prose.

sources.name: DEQ Water Quality Monitoring Stations
known_limitations:
NOT a complete inventory of environmental sites. These are DEQ's water-quality monitoring stations, active and historic. A location with no station near it has no DEQ monitoring station near it, and that is the whole of what the absence means.
A station is not a finding. Its presence says DEQ monitors or has monitored that spot; it says nothing about whether anything was found, whether a site is contaminated, or whether ground is safe or suitable for any use.
Historic stations are included. LAST_SAMPLE_DATE can be decades old, so a station in a result is not evidence of current monitoring. Read the per-station dates.
The layer carries no locality or FIPS field. It is organised by watershed (HUC) and DEQ administrative region, so a query is scoped by geography and never by jurisdiction, and results near a boundary can belong to a neighbouring locality.
Water quality only. DEQ also regulates air, waste, and land, and none of those programmes is in this layer or this registration.

sources.name: eVA (Virginia procurement)
sources.publisher: Virginia Department of General Services, Division of Purchases and Supply
known_limitations:
No endpoint discovery has run. Whether eVA exposes solicitations or awards through anything other than its own web UI is an open question, not a recorded finding.
Procurement records name private parties, so the data-classification review here is a real one rather than a formality — an award record is public, a losing bidder's contact details may not be.

sources.name: Fairfax County Parcels and Zoning (Open Data)
sources.publisher: Fairfax County government (GIS and Mapping Services, Open Data)
known_limitations: GIS zoning is a screening representation; the adopted zoning ordinance and official zoning map govern.
Neither layer publishes a machine-readable last-edit date.

sources.name: Virginia Open Data Portal (CKAN)
sources.publisher: Virginia Office of Data Governance and Analytics
known_limitations:
Verified 2026-08-29: CKAN 2.9.11 with the Action API reachable anonymously (`/api/3/action/status_show` returns 200), 64 publishing organizations.
This is a catalog, not a data source. Its records describe other agencies' datasets; a query against it answers "who published something about X", never "what is at this address". The capability it would answer is dataset discovery, which overlaps `registry.search_sources` and needs a design decision before a tool, not just a manifest.
Most resources are file downloads (CSV, shapefile) rather than queryable services, so onboarding one of them means the download question decision 0006 defers, not another ArcGIS registration.

sources.name: Richmond City Parcels and Zoning (GIS Open Data)
sources.publisher: City of Richmond (Information Technology / Assessor of Real Estate)
known_limitations: GIS zoning is a screening representation; the adopted zoning ordinance and official zoning map govern.
Parcels layer stacks multiple ownership records under one geometry for multi-owner PINs (see the CountOfPIN field in the publisher's schema).

sources.name: State Corporation Commission (business entities and utilities)
known_limitations:
No endpoint discovery has run. The Clerk's Information System is a session-based web application, which is the shape most likely to have no public API at all and the shape this project's egress policy is least willing to work around.
Business-entity records name registered agents at their own addresses. That is public by statute and still a sensitive_public classification question, reviewed before anything activates.

sources.name: Virginia Department of Health (no queryable endpoint found)
known_limitations:
Checked 2026-08-29. `gis.vdh.virginia.gov` does not resolve (NXDOMAIN), so the ArcGIS REST directory the other state publishers expose has no VDH equivalent.
Checked 2026-08-29. VDH does publish through the state open-data portal: 144 datasets under the `virginia-department-of-health` organization on data.virginia.gov. Every resource sampled is a CSV download of an aggregate public-use dataset (COVID-19, mpox, healthcare-associated infections, heat-related illness), not a record-shaped service that answers a query about a place or a facility. A bulk CSV is a real publication and a poor fit for a capability whose contract is "look this up".
Checked 2026-08-29. No licensed-facility or inspection registry with an API surfaced under VDH. Health-professional licensing sits with the Department of Health Professions, a separate agency and a separate future manifest, not this one.
Absence of an endpoint is not absence of data. This row exists so the gap is inventory rather than memory, and re-checking it is a re-verification of this manifest rather than a fresh search.

sources.name: VDOT Route Master (LRS)
known_limitations:
A linear-referencing route model, not a centerline topology. A route is a named linear feature with official state measures; it is not an edge between two intersections and route records do not correspond one-to-one with centerline segments.
RTE_JURIS_CD is VDOT's own jurisdiction numbering and is NOT a FIPS code. Observed live 2026-08-29: City of Manassas is "155", City of Suffolk "133". Do not join it to federal data.
RTE_JURIS_PROPER_NM is null on about 6,500 of the 196,896 routes (190,372 populated, read live 2026-08-29), largely the interstate and frontage-road records that span localities. Those are missed by a jurisdiction-scoped query and found by a proximity one.
Covers routes VDOT maintains a linear reference for. Roads maintained entirely by a locality may be absent, which is not evidence the road does not exist — it is what the two registered road sources exist to show each other.

sources.name: Virginia Address Points (VGIN)
sources.publisher: Virginia Geographic Information Network (VGIN), part of the Virginia Department of Emergency Management
known_limitations:
Cartographic/analysis use only per the publisher's own disclaimer; an address point is not a legal description or a survey.
Aggregated from local submissions on the data-call cycle, so currency varies by locality. A locality that has submitted nothing since its last call is covered by the registry and stale in the layer, which are two different facts.
PO_NAME is a postal city, not a government. Verified live 2026-08-29: 4501 CARLBY LN in Fairfax County carries PO_NAME "ALEXANDRIA", an independent city it is not in. Only FIPS and MUNICIPALITY name a jurisdiction here.
PLACENAME is NOT a postal place, despite the name, and mapping it as one would have been wrong. Read live 2026-08-29, its populated values are landmark and facility names — "Rose Hill Elementary School", "ABC Store 099", "DMV Customer Service Center Fairfax" — and it is empty for ordinary residential addresses. It is mapped as `landmark_name` for that reason.
An address absent from this layer is not evidence that no such address exists. A locality behind on its data call, a new subdivision, and a genuinely invented address all look identical here.
Address-string matching is an exact or prefix match on the publisher's own FULLADDR spelling ("6800 BEULAH ST"), not a fuzzy search. Use the composite locator (geo.resolve_location) when the input is a typed address that needs interpreting.

sources.name: Virginia Administrative Boundaries (VGIN)
sources.publisher: Virginia Geographic Information Network (VGIN), part of the Virginia Department of Emergency Management
known_limitations: Cartographic/analysis use only per the publisher's own disclaimer; not a legal description or a property survey. Boundary questions with legal consequence go to the locality, not this layer.

Layer publishes no layer-level last-edit date (editingInfo is absent on both layers), so envelope source_updated_at is null. The per-record LASTUPDATE field IS mapped and surfaced per boundary, so each returned record carries its own vintage even though the layer does not.

Geometry is returned simplified (server-side generalization) so a polygon fits an inline response; the unsimplified boundary is not exposed until the result-resource store exists. Simplified vertices can sit tens of metres off the true line — never use them to decide which side of a boundary a specific address falls on.

The localities layer carries 134 rows for Virginia's 133 counties and independent cities. Prince George County (FIPS 51149) is published as two separate polygons sharing one FIPS and GNIS, a 281 sq mi body and a 0.0076 sq mi sliver. Both are returned; neither is silently dropped. See ../../design/source-quirks.md.
Towns layer covers incorporated towns only. Virginia's unincorporated communities and CDPs have no polygon here, and absence is not evidence that a place does not exist.

sources.name: Virginia Building Footprints (VGIN)
sources.publisher: Virginia Geographic Information Network (VGIN), part of the Virginia Department of Emergency Management
known_limitations:
Cartographic/analysis use only per the publisher's own disclaimer; a footprint is not a survey and not a legal description.
Derived and aggregated from local submissions and other sources (DATASOURCENAME says which per record), so both coverage and vintage vary by locality.
A missing footprint is not evidence of vacant land. A locality that has not submitted, a structure built since the last update, and genuinely empty ground all look identical here.
Shape__Area is in the layer's own Web Mercator projection, where area is inflated by roughly sec squared of the latitude — about 1.6x at Virginia's latitudes. It is returned unconverted under a field name that says which projection it is in, alongside an approximate ground area derived from the query's own latitude and declared in the envelope's transformations.
BLDGHEIGHT, NUMSTORIES, BUILDINGCLASS, and FEATURECODE are sparse. Observed live 2026-08-29 in downtown Richmond: all four null on every footprint sampled, with only geometry, FIPS, MUNICIPALITY, DATASOURCENAME, and LASTUPDATE populated. Null means the publisher has no value, not that the building has no storeys.
A dense urban query returns hundreds of polygons and the service caps the response. The 25-record inline cap and truncated pagination apply; narrow the radius rather than reading a truncated list as the whole answer.

sources.name: Virginia Composite Locator (VGIN Geocoding Service)
sources.publisher: Virginia Geographic Information Network (VGIN), part of the Virginia Department of Emergency Management
known_limitations:
Virginia only. The publisher states the service "cannot guarantee results in other states"; an out-of-state address is not a failure of the address, it is outside what this locator covers.
A composite locator falls back down a hierarchy: address points first, then road centerlines, then city/state, CAI, GNIS, ZIP codes, and finally jurisdictions. A ZIP-code match is a centroid, not the address — matched_by and address_type say which element answered, and a caller that ignores them will treat a ZIP centroid as a rooftop.
The locator's own City attribute is a POSTAL city, not a government. Observed 2026-08-29, a Fairfax County address in ZIP 22310 returns City "ALEXANDRIA", which is an independent city it is not in. Never read it as the jurisdiction.
Subregion is inconsistent between the locator's elements. Observed 2026-08-29 for the same query: the road-centerline element returned the FIPS code "51059" and the address-point element returned the name "Fairfax County". It is returned as data and never parsed.
A ZIP code geocodes to one centroid, which for a ZIP spanning several localities is an answer to a question nobody asked. geo.resolve_location does not use this path for ZIPs; it queries the address-point layer for every locality the ZIP touches.

sources.name: Virginia Landmark Locations (VGIN)
sources.publisher: Virginia Geographic Information Network (VGIN), part of the Virginia Department of Emergency Management
known_limitations:
A curated convenience layer, not an inventory. Absence proves nothing: a school, library, or fire station missing from it may simply never have been added.
Records cite third parties. Src names the organisation the record came from (DCJS, DOE, USPS, "Agency" among them) and it is that organisation, not VGIN, whose record a landmark actually is.
LastCheck is null on many records. Where it is null the record says so rather than inheriting the layer's date, because "nobody has re-checked this" and "checked today" are different facts.
URL values are returned as data and never fetched. The egress allowlist is per manifest and following a link found inside a record would drive straight through it.
City is a postal city, not a government. FIPScode and FIPSname are what name the jurisdiction.
PlaceType is the publisher's own vocabulary, 33 values observed live 2026-08-29 ("Law Enforcement Points", "Schools Public K12 Points", "ABC Store Points" and so on). It is returned verbatim; there is no mapping onto a general category scheme.

sources.name: Virginia Road Centerlines (VGIN VBMP RCL)
sources.publisher: Virginia Geographic Information Network (VGIN), part of the Virginia Department of Emergency Management
known_limitations:
Cartographic/analysis use only per the publisher's own disclaimer; a centerline is not a right-of-way boundary or a survey.
Aggregated from local government submissions on the data-call cycle, so currency varies by locality.
Registration queries layer 4 only. Verified live 2026-08-29, that is the complete 659,179-segment feature class; layer 5 is the same data at a different map scale and layers 1 and 2 are road-class subsets of it, so nothing is excluded by the choice.
A road along a locality line has different FIPS on its two sides. Jurisdiction filtering matches EITHER side, so such a road is returned for both localities. That is correct and it means a result is not evidence the road lies wholly inside one.
SEG_TYPE, MTFCC, and SEG_EXISTS are publisher codes with no coded- value domain published on the layer, so they are returned raw with their field names intact rather than given invented labels.

sources.name: Virginia Statewide Parcels (VGIN)
sources.publisher: Virginia Geographic Information Network (VGIN), part of the Virginia Department of Emergency Management
known_limitations: Cartographic/analysis use only per the publisher's own disclaimer; not a legal description or survey.
Parcel boundaries are not edge-matched across municipal boundaries.
Currency varies by locality and lags the locality's own live system; this is the statewide fallback, not the fast path, for any jurisdiction that also has a local manifest.
No zoning equivalent published statewide; parcel.lookup only.
Layer publishes no machine-readable last-edit date at the layer level (a per-record LASTUPDATE field exists but is not exposed through this adapter's freshness path).

skills.name: development-site-due-diligence
skills.status: deferred until there is coverage to justify it

registry.question: Does the Source Registry cover the requested place/capability/time at all?

values.covered: A registered source should answer this.
values.partial: Some but not all of what was asked is covered.
values.none: No source is registered for this place. The answer says so, and says which place it means.

execution.question: Did the queries that should have run actually finish?

values.complete: Every source that should have been queried was.
values.partial: Named sources could not be checked; the answer says which.
values.failed: The call failed outright; the typed error rides alongside this envelope.

pagination.question: Was the record set fully paged?

values.truncated: The source's own transfer limit cut the result short (ArcGIS exceededTransferLimit). The answer is labelled as partial.
values.unknown: Paging completeness could not be determined.

values.empty: The search ran and matched nothing. That is a result, and it is reported separately from a failure.

warning_definitions.screening_only: GIS zoning is a screening layer. The adopted zoning ordinance and official zoning map govern; confirm before any legal reliance.
warning_definitions.stale_source: The source's own update cadence was missed.
warning_definitions.freshness_unavailable: The publisher gives no machine-readable update date for this layer. The fetch time is known; how old the data itself is cannot be established.
warning_definitions.boundary_precision: Parcel or boundary geometry is generalized, not surveyed.
warning_definitions.alias_match: The entity matched via a registered alias, not its exact id.
warning_definitions.mixed_vintages: Results combine records with different as-of dates.
warning_definitions.terms_note: The source's terms constrain reuse of this data.
warning_definitions.sensitive_public_data: The source is classified sensitive_public: technically public, but redistribution is field-allowlisted and reviewed before the source may go active.
warning_definitions.insecure_transport: This source is reached over plain HTTP, per a reviewed manifest exception, not HTTPS.
warning_definitions.truncated_inline: More records were retrieved than are shown inline; narrow the query for the rest.
